Contributing to Callisto

By participating in this project, you agree to abide by the [Code of Conduct](./CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md). Found a security issue? See [SECURITY.md](./SECURITY.md) instead of opening a public issue. Agent-specific rules (invariants, fixing-bugs workflow, specs/plans, crate/license table) live in [AGENTS.md](./AGENTS.md) — this file covers human setup and PR process and does not duplicate them. How the code fits together: [ARCHITECTURE.md](./ARCHITECTURE.md) and [docs/architecture/](./docs/architecture/). --- ## Setup - Rust toolchain: pinned in `rust-toolchain.toml`, installed via `rustup`. - [`just`](https://github.com/casey/just): command runner for all workspace recipes. - Cargo tools the recipes call: `cargo-nextest`, `cargo-llvm-cov`, `cargo-deny`, `cargo-machete` and `cargo-semver-checks`. - Workflow linters `zizmor` and `actionlint`: tests that lint the workflow `callisto init` generates run them. A missing one skips the check on your machine and fails the test under CI. - [`moon`](https://moonrepo.dev): a few recipes (`build`, `fmt`, `fmt-check`, `lint-affected`) delegate to it; installed like any other tool via [proto](https://moonrepo.dev/proto) (`proto/callisto.toml` shows the same pattern for installing `callisto` itself). ```bash git clone https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto.git cd callisto just hooks # installs .git/hooks/pre-commit and pre-push just ci # full local verification pipeline ``` --- ## `just` recipes | Command | Runs | | :--- | :--- | | `just ci` | Everything CI runs except Docker-based actionlint and the binary-dependent release-PR/artifact-preflight jobs: `fmt-check lint test audit doc-check zizmor workflow-contracts release-workflow-behavior coverage 90` | | `just build` | Debug workspace binaries, via `moon run :build` | | `just build-release` | `cargo build --release -p callisto-cli` | | `just test` | `cargo nextest run --workspace` + `cargo test --doc --workspace`; this is what CI runs | | `just test-moon` | Compatibility path via `moon run :test` for contributors without `cargo-nextest`; never used by CI | | `just lint` | `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` | | `just lint-affected` | Clippy scoped to crates affected since the base branch (via `moon query projects --affected`) | | `just fmt-check` / `just fmt` | Formatting check / apply, via `moon run :format-check` / `:format` | | `just audit` | `cargo deny check` (advisories, bans, licenses, sources) | | `just doc-check` | `cargo doc --no-deps --workspace` with warnings as errors | | `just coverage [threshold]` | `cargo llvm-cov` workspace report to `lcov.info`; `just coverage 90` is what CI's `coverage` job and `just ci` both call, so a coverage failure always reproduces locally | | `just coverage-per-crate [threshold]` | Same profile data, gated per crate instead of workspace-total; CI runs it blocking at 90 | | `just machete` | Unused dependencies (`cargo machete`); CI runs it | | `just features-boundary` | Fails if the dev-only `test-util` feature reaches the shipped `callisto-cli` build; CI runs it | | `just check-api` | Public API compared with the published crates (`cargo semver-checks`); CI runs it on the release PR, where versions have moved | | `just bench` | Wall time and process counts for `status`, `version --dry-run` and `release --dry-run` over generated workspaces | | `just fuzz-check` | Compiles the fuzz targets so they cannot rot; CI runs it | | `just zizmor` | Static security audit of workflow/action YAML (requires `zizmor`) | | `just workflow-contracts` | Release-workflow contract/policy tests, action pin verification, installer tests — what the CI `workflow-contracts` job runs besides actionlint | | `just release-workflow-behavior` | Release lifecycle exercised at the real CLI boundary with faked registry/Git/forge/attestation providers | | `just pre-commit` | `fmt-check` only — fast, runs on every local commit via the installed hook | | `just pre-push` | `fmt-check` + `lint-affected` — runs on every local push via the installed hook | | `just hooks` | Installs the native `pre-commit`/`pre-push` git hooks above | | `just clean` | Clears moon task caches, `cargo clean`, removes `lcov.info` / `callisto-schema.json` | Maintainer-only recipes not part of the normal PR loop: `mutants` (mutation testing), `fuzz` (runs a fuzz target; needs nightly and `cargo-fuzz`), `provider-fixtures`/`provider-contract` (re-capture/verify the real-provider test fixtures under `testing/fixtures/`). A weekly workflow (`callisto-quality.yml`, also runnable by hand) fuzzes the four parser targets for ten minutes each and runs mutation testing over `callisto-model` and `callisto-manifests` in six shards. Both report and never block a merge: a crash uploads its input as an artifact, and the surviving mutants of each shard are listed in its job summary. A surviving mutant is a change that passes every test, so each one is either a missing test or dead code. For iterating on one crate instead of the whole workspace, see AGENTS.md's scoped-iteration guidance (`cargo test -p `, one invocation at a time — never parallel cargo builds). --- ## Changesets Non-interactive, for scripts, agents, and most contributors: ```bash callisto add --package cargo/: --summary "..." ``` `--package` takes repeatable `ecosystem/name:severity` pairs (`none`, `patch`, `minor`, `major`). The summary is the changelog entry users will read. Write it by the changeset rules in [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md#changesets). Callisto puts each summary under a version heading as one bullet. Nested bullets in the summary stay nested in the changelog. Interactive wizard (omit `--package`/`--summary`, run from a TTY): prompts for packages, then major-bump packages, then minor-bump packages (rest default to patch), then a summary, then a confirmation preview before writing `.changeset/.md`. ```bash cargo run --bin callisto -- add ``` --- ## PR checklist CI (`.github/workflows/callisto-ci.yml`) gates on: - **`fmt`** — `just fmt-check` - **`clippy`** — `just lint` + `just doc-check` - **`test`** — `just test`, `just release-workflow-behavior`, the Release-PR action's binary contract test, and the problem matcher test, on Linux and macOS - **`release-artifact-preflight`** — builds the release binary for each configured target (macOS arm64 and x64, Linux x64 gnu, arm64 gnu and x64 musl) - **`coverage`** — `just coverage 90` (workspace line coverage must not regress below 90%) and `just coverage-per-crate 90` (each crate too) - **`hygiene`** — `just machete`, `just features-boundary`, and on the release PR `just check-api` - **`security`** — `just audit` - **`validate`** — changeset and workspace-status validation - **`release-asset-attestation`** — downloads the latest release's Linux asset with CI's read-only token and verifies its attestation (same-repo PRs and pushes to main only; skipped when no release exists) - **`workflow-contracts`** — actionlint, zizmor, action pin verification (every external action pinned to a full commit, and one commit per action across `.github` and the generated-workflow templates), and the release-workflow contract/policy tests Tests earn their place by covering a behavior, an edge case or an error state, not a line. A change that adds a diagnostic code also adds its row to [docs/errors.md](docs/errors.md); a test fails without it. Before opening a PR: run `just ci` locally and make sure `just pre-push` is clean. `just ci` covers the format, lint, test, security and workflow-contract jobs and the 90% workspace coverage; the `hygiene` recipes (`just machete`, `just features-boundary`, `just check-api`), per-crate coverage, the MSRV check, changeset validation and the artifact preflight run only in CI. Add a changeset for any user-facing change (see above). Before 1.0, a change that breaks a public Rust item in any crate needs a `minor` changeset, or `just check-api` fails on the release PR. Follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) for commit messages. ## Merging to main The `main` ruleset requires one approving review, signed commits, squash merges and every CI job passing. Merging a release PR publishes it; there is no second approval. The owner's ruleset bypass is for emergency recovery only. (eval):1: ===== not found

# Contributing

By participating in this project, you agree to abide by the [Code of Conduct](./CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md). Found a security issue? See [SECURITY.md](./SECURITY.md) instead of opening a public issue.

## Prerequisites

| Tool  | Min version | Notes                                         |
| ----- | ----------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| Rust  | 1.97        | `rustup update stable`                        |
| proto | latest      | manages Node/pnpm versions from `.prototools` |
| pnpm  | 9           | via proto, or `npm i -g pnpm`                 |

After installing proto, run `moon setup` once to pull the pinned Node version and any other tool versions declared in `.prototools`.

## Build & test

```bash
# Rust
cargo build                                            # dev build
cargo test -p caliper-docgen-core                   # unit + snapshot tests
cargo clippy -p caliper-docgen-core -- -D warnings
cargo fmt --all

# TypeScript
pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-vite-plugin test      # 33 unit tests (mocked NAPI)
pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-vite-plugin test:integration  # 3 integration tests (real native binding)

# Speed and memory of your branch against origin/main (Mantine and Chakra)
just bench
```

The pre-commit hook runs `cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings`, `typos`, and `cargo deny` on every commit. It's fast enough that skipping it isn't worth the trouble.

## Snapshot tests

Snapshot tests use [insta](https://insta.rs). Each fixture (shadcn, MUI, Chakra, etc.) has a snapshot of the full extraction output. If your change touches extraction output, insta will flag it:

```bash
cargo test -p caliper-docgen-core    # fails with "snapshot mismatch"
cargo insta review                     # review diffs, accept or reject
```

Accept any snapshot change that is intentional (i.e., the output got more accurate). Reject regressions.

## Where code goes

**`crates/core`** — everything that understands TypeScript ASTs and React component patterns. No I/O, no async, no terminal output. Every function here must be `Send + Sync` so rayon can parallelize it.

**`crates/cli`** — user-facing output only. No extraction logic. Commands parse args and delegate to `core::pipeline`. Error formatting uses `miette`; progress uses `indicatif`; table output uses `comfy-table`.

**`crates/binding`** — thin NAPI wrapper. Owns the async runtime (tokio) and exposes the NAPI functions listed in `packages/napi/binding.d.ts` (batch extraction, sessions, and the lazy session's index, answers and warm-up). No business logic.

**`packages/napi`** — `caliper-docgen-napi`. TypeScript types (`index.d.ts`) and the dev binary loader (`index.js`) that finds the `.node` file from `target/` or `NAPI_RS_NATIVE_LIBRARY_PATH`. No logic.

**`packages/vite-plugin`** — `caliper-docgen-vite-plugin`. Single Vite `Plugin` object. No extraction logic — calls NAPI and manages HMR.

## Code style

The authoritative reference is `.claude/skills/rust-style/SKILL.md`. Highlights:

**Maps:** `FxHashMap` for internal maps (hot path, no DoS surface). `BTreeMap` for anything that ends up in JSON output (key ordering must be deterministic and stable across runs).

**Strings:** `CompactString` for type names and prop names. Most are ≤24 bytes (`string`, `boolean`, `ReactNode`, `MouseEvent`) and fit inline without heap allocation.

**Control flow:** `let...else` keeps the happy path flat:

```rust
let Some(entry) = map.get(key) else { return None };
```

**Matching on project-local enums:** no wildcards. `match status { Ok => .., Err => .. }` gives a compile error when new variants are added. `match status { Ok => .., _ => .. }` silently ignores them.

**No `unwrap()` outside tests.** Use `?` or emit a `Diagnostic` and return a safe default. The `Diagnostic` type has constructors for common error shapes.

**Comments:** only when the WHY is non-obvious. Not what the code does.

## Commits

- GPG-signed, `Signed-off-by` trailer (both configured in `.git/config`). `main` requires signed commits, so an unsigned commit in a pull request blocks the merge.
- `feat:` / `fix:` / `refactor:` / `chore:` / `docs:` prefix
- No line wrapping at any column
- Subject line says it all — skip the body if it adds nothing

```
# good
feat: resolve ComponentPropsWithoutRef in intersection type aliases

# bad
Updated the resolver to also handle the case where ComponentPropsWithoutRef
appears inside an intersection type alias, which was causing it to be
treated as opaque when it should expand the HTML attributes.
```

## Releases

Add a changeset for a consumer-visible change (`.changeset/`; see `AGENTS.md` for how to write one). Callisto 0.16 plans the versions from the changesets and opens a release pull request (`callisto/version-packages`); merging it runs `.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml`, which publishes the crates and npm packages, tags each package, and publishes one GitHub Release for the CLI (`cargo/caliper-docgen@x.y.z`) with its changelog section as the notes and the five CLI binaries attached, each with a build attestation. The npm wrapper's tag `npm/caliper-docgen@x.y.z` is what the tap reads. `docs/releasing.md` has the release flow and how to recover a failed run.

Homebrew pulls from us: the tap's daily `brew bump` finds that tag with `livecheck`, builds `crates/cli` from source and bottles it, and a maintainer merges the formula pull request. Nothing in this repository notifies the tap.

Speed, memory and accuracy are recorded weekly and compared with the previous run (`docs/measurement.md`); there is no pull-request gate. Run `just bench` when a change touches the resolver.

## Pull requests

1. Branch from `main`
2. Keep the pre-commit hook passing
3. Update snapshots if extraction output changes (`cargo insta review`)
4. One logical change per PR — squash fixup commits before merging

> `just bench` is a local check of speed and memory against `main`; it prints a table and fails nothing. Accuracy against RDT and react-docgen is tracked by the weekly record (`docs/measurement.md`), not by a pull-request gate.

# crates/core

Pure extraction logic — no terminal, no NAPI, no async. Everything here must be `Send + Sync` for rayon.

## Module layout

```
types/          — shared data types (the contract between phases)
extractor/      — OXC AST visitor → SourceData
resolver/       — SourceData + GlobalSourceData → ComponentEntry
pipeline/       — orchestration: discover → parse → merge → resolve
cache.rs        — DTS parse cache (mtime+size invalidation, msgpack)
import_map.rs   — import resolution map
known.rs        — library-specific type shortcuts (SxProps, VariantProps…)
react_types.rs  — React builtin recognition + notable HTML attrs
```

## Types discipline

When adding a public type, run through the checklist in the `rust-types` skill. Canonical reference: `src/types/diagnostic.rs`.

## Resolver

`resolve_component()` is called in parallel via rayon. All inputs must be owned or `Arc`-wrapped — no borrowed data crosses thread boundaries. `ResolveState` accumulates diagnostics and visited-type tracking for a single resolution call; it is not shared.

## Panic containment

Anything reachable from a rayon `.map()` or a `DocgenPlugin` impl must go through `panic_guard::contain_panic` — see `pipeline/mod.rs` and `plugin.rs` for the call sites, and `docs/adr/0005-panic-containment-boundary.md` for why.

## Snapshot tests

Seven fixtures in `crates/core/tests/snapshots/`. If a change affects output, regenerate with `/snapshot` before committing.
# crates/cli

Thin command layer — no extraction logic. Each command parses args and delegates to `caliper-docgen-core::pipeline`.

## Layout

```
main.rs              — Cli struct, Command enum, *Args structs, main(), init_tracing()
commands/            — one file per subcommand (extract, watch, inspect, check, completions)
config.rs            — docgen.config.ts loading, maps to PipelineOptions
output.rs            — comfy-table formatting helpers
```

## Rules

Command payloads go to stdout with `println!`; diagnostics, progress and everything on stderr go through `output.rs` or the tracing subscriber — never `eprintln!`. Error display uses `miette`. Progress uses `indicatif`.

Config loading (`config.rs`) runs the user's `docgen.config.ts` via node+tsx. The config file path is passed via env var, not embedded in a shell string — command injection risk otherwise.
# List available commands
default:
    @just --list

# Install the cargo tools the recipes below use
install-tools:
    cargo install cargo-nextest cargo-llvm-cov cargo-machete cargo-mutants cargo-deny typos-cli zizmor --locked
    rustup component add llvm-tools-preview

# Install the pinned toolchain and the moon-managed git hooks
setup:
    proto install
    moon sync vcs-hooks

# Build the workspace. One `cargo --workspace` invocation, not `moon run :build`: per-crate cargo processes all
# contend for the same target/ lock and serialize.
build:
    cargo build --workspace --locked

build-release:
    cargo build --workspace --release --locked

# Run tests with nextest, plus doctests, which nextest does not run. The default-features pass catches code that only
# builds because --all-features turned something on.
test:
    cargo nextest run --workspace --all-features --locked
    cargo nextest run --workspace --locked
    cargo test --doc --workspace --all-features --locked

# Line coverage; fails below the threshold, which this default owns
coverage threshold="90":
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    cargo llvm-cov nextest --workspace --all-features --locked --lcov --output-path lcov.info
    cargo llvm-cov report --summary-only --fail-under-lines "{{ threshold }}"

# Coverage report, opened in the browser
coverage-html:
    cargo llvm-cov nextest --workspace --all-features --locked --html --open

# Format check, clippy with and without default features, and typos, the same as CI's lint job
lint: typos
    cargo fmt --all --check
    cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings
    cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --no-default-features --locked -- -D warnings

# Clippy on the crates moon reports as affected, in one cargo invocation
lint-affected:
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    projects=$(moon query projects --affected | jq -r '.projects[].id')
    if [ -z "$projects" ]; then exit 0; fi
    args=()
    for p in $projects; do args+=(-p "$p"); done
    cargo clippy "${args[@]}" --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings

fmt:
    cargo fmt --all

# Documentation build, with warnings (including broken intra-doc links) as errors
doc-check:
    RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --no-deps --workspace --all-features --locked
    RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --no-deps --workspace --locked

# Licenses, advisories, bans and sources
deny:
    cargo deny check

# Unused dependencies
machete:
    cargo machete

typos:
    typos

# Callisto config, package discovery and pending changesets; the same gate as CI's Changesets job
changesets:
    callisto status --check --strict
    callisto release --dry-run --format text

# Record a pending change for the next release, e.g. `just changeset minor "Add the search command"`
changeset bump summary:
    callisto add --package cargo/monokl:{{ bump }} --summary "{{ summary }}"

# Workflow audit for permission, credential and supply-chain issues
zizmor:
    zizmor --offline --strict-collection .

# Fails when a duplicated fact disagrees with its owner, e.g. the Callisto pin in the workflows against .prototools
check-drift:

# dependencies; `package.json` carries the same verbs for pnpm. See "Commands" in AGENTS.md.

# List available commands
default:
    @just --list

# Install the toolchain (node, pnpm, moon via proto), dependencies and git hooks. `just` itself is not a proto tool:
# see the README for its one-line install.
setup:
    proto install
    pnpm install
    moon sync vcs-hooks

# Build the Panda packages and all three sites
build:
    moon run :build

# Run one dev server: techworx (4322), orin-dx (4321) or orin-dx-docs (4324), always on the LAN (--host 0.0.0.0).
# `just dev sb` runs both Storybooks (6006 and 6007). Without a site, list the sites that have a dev server.
dev site="":
    @if [ -z "{{ site }}" ]; then \
        echo "Pass a site: just dev <site>"; \
        moon query tasks "task=dev" | node -e 'console.log(Object.keys(JSON.parse(require("fs").readFileSync(0, "utf8")).tasks).map((id) => `  ${id}`).join("\n"))'; \

storybook brand:

preview site:

typecheck:

lint:

# techworx.dev agent guide

The site is Gabe Castro's portfolio. Its job is to get Gabe hired into a staff role and to share his work. It is a confident portfolio where the work is the proof, never a pitch: no "open to roles", no call-to-action bands.

## Sources of truth

- **Design rules:** the brand package at `packages/brand/techworx/project/` (read `packages/brand/AGENTS.md` first), published as the techworx.dev design system on claude.ai. Read `views.md` (light and dark), `colour.md`, `type-and-space.md`, `layout.md`, `interface.md`, `icons.md`, `identity.md` and `voice.md` before changing how the site looks or reads.
- **The claude.ai design system** (techworx.dev, https://claude.ai/artifact/Ae2GuQ6H9WfhPXyUdTnHrt) uses the site's own CSS and components. After changing a twx recipe, component or token, build the site (`pnpm --filter techworx build`), run `pnpm --filter @pages/twx design-system` to regenerate the library's `components/bundle.css`, `bundle.js` and previews, then publish the library's `project/` folder to the artifact. Designs made in Claude then match the site.
- **Tokens:** `packages/brand/techworx/project/tokens.json` is the source, roles included. Edit it there, run `cd packages/brand && npx vitest run`, and Panda reads it through `packages/foundations`. There are no copies to refresh.
- **Writing:** `docs/plans/writing-system.md`.
- **Decision history:** the "Design proposals and reviews" canvas on claude.ai. Each decision has a short code, such as A, K2, R3 or Kn1, and the library docs cite the code next to each rule.

## Rules that are easy to break

- **Light and dark change colour only (A).** Never switch fonts, artwork, icon weight or list order by theme. `preview` (light) and `outline` (dark) are internal theme names only. Don't use Preview or Outline in copy.
- **Red is for things you act on (R3).** Download links and the location point. Measurement marks in figures use `text.measure` (body ink), never red. Buttons and controls are ink, not red (owner, 2026-10-12). Kickers, the now line and tags are `text.muted`.
- **Kinds are labels (K2).** Engineering is teal, design amber, writing violet, and notes green (Kn1). Use the `kind.*` roles for kind words, glyphs and group rules only. Never use them for fills, buttons or links.
- **One reading frame (Wd).** The page is 1256px: rails of 200px, gaps of 48px and a reading column of 760px. Everything in a reading page fills the column.
- **The rails open one at a time, as on Orin DX (Rl).** One column below 760px of container, with the chapters in the nav sheet. The left rail opens from 760px, with notes still inline. Both rails open from 1304px. Components follow these states through the `_oneColumn`, `_leftRail`, `_bothRails` and `_notesInline` conditions. Never restate the widths, and never use `_rail` (1104px) for anything that depends on where notes sit.
- **Lint.** `just lint` runs oxlint with the Panda rules, and `just format` checks formatting with oxfmt. The Panda plugin does not check `defineRecipe` or `defineSlotRecipe`, so keep recipes to the same rules by hand: logical properties, tokens, no `!important`.
- **One primary action per page.** On the home page it is "Read the CV" (H1).
- **Motifs.** The dot grid with one red point and the glow are the only motifs. On a page with a rail, the dots sit over the margin column only (D1). Project covers and post covers are artwork and are exempt.
- **No stages.** Work and writing carry no stage (St). Writing publishes finished posts only, with no public drafts and no comment links.
- **Page rules.** Openers sit 48px (`gap.block`) under the nav, on every width, chapters are separated by space and not rules, and a document's hero runs the page's width over the rails: `docs/plans/page-layouts.md`, "Decided in review". A specimen of a real component is the real component, or a copy kept in step.
- **The CV layout is locked.** Only align its edges to the grid.
- **Never use Gabe's former name** anywhere on the site.

## Post covers

Every post has a cover made of up to three layers. The full rules are in the library's `identity.md` (Post covers) and `voice.md` (Covers). In short:

- **Layers.**
  - A **field** shows behaviour and is always the ground. Its marks are dots, streams, contours or strata; streams are many fine lines in the topic colour, drawn with the strand engine in `@pages/foundations/strands` (the one Orin's ribbon uses): loose at the left and settling toward the right, no red point, one line per thing the post counts. A field is artwork, so it adds no motif to the page.
  - **Type** sets the claim: a word or number quoted from the post.
  - A **plate** draws the mechanism, hatched with the field's own marks.
- **Which layer leads.**
  - An argument leads with type.
  - A measurement leads with the field.
  - How a system works leads with a plate.
  - Design craft leads with a plate, supported by type.
  - A series shares one plate.
  - A note gets a field from config, or no cover.
- **Composition.** One layer leads. Use two layers by default and three only for a featured post or a series opener.
- **Material.** Use only the post's real names and numbers. If the cover could belong to another post, it isn't finished.
- **Size check.** The cover must still read at 160×100.
- **Files.** Deliver 1600×1000 light and dark masters, a plate detail crop and a 1200×630 share crop. Keep the cover's source beside the post.

New creative work, including a new cover, needs Gabe's approval before it goes on a page.

## Figures in a case study

- **One frame per figure.** The frame is the only box: artwork is cropped clean inside it, with no border, radius, gutter sliver or baked-in square of its own. A figure that differs by theme is one frame with the Light and Dark switch, not two images.
- **The frame speaks techworx; the art speaks its own system.** Never put techworx's red or kind colours on another system's artwork, and never draw a third colour onto it.
- **Mark a chosen option in the frame, then by dimming.** The chosen option gets an ink hairline, the red point and the word "Chosen" in its caption, so colour never carries it alone. In a decision's option set the others sit back at 0.6 (`dimOthers` on `CaseRounds`); a timeline of rounds does not dim.
- **Point from outside.** To annotate a detail, use `Callouts`: numbered mono pills on the frame edge with a key, never in the artwork's colours and never red.
- **Read the system, don't retype it.** Colour roles, ladders, type styles and gaps come from the token sources through `data/systemFigures.ts`; the figure components (`RoleLayers`, `RoleLadder`, `TypeRows`, `RoomDemo`, `BeforeAfter`) never take a hand-written value.

## Tests

Write behaviour tests: rendering, order, focus, mode changes and contrast that a decision relies on. Don't add tests that pin colours, sizes or positions while a design is still changing. Check the result with screenshots in both modes, on desktop and at 390px.
# Brand package agent guide

Read `README.md` first. This file is the steps; the reasoning is in `docs/brand/principles/` (start with `shared.md`).

## Change a token

1. Edit `packages/brand/<brand>/project/tokens.json` (`orin` or `techworx`). It is the source: Panda reads it, and the Claude design system artifact is published from it.
2. Keep the artifact format. Every family except `type` is `{"tokens": [{name, value, usage}]}`, a list. Colour also has `themes`. Never write a name-to-value map.
3. Names match `[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]{0,63}` and are unique across every family except `type`. Give every token a `usage` note that says where it is used.
4. Colour values are hex, `rgb()`, `rgba()`, `hsl()`, `hsla()` or `oklch()` with no function inside, or an alias `"{other-token}"` of an existing colour token. Never use `var()`, `color-mix()` or a named colour (`red`, `transparent`, `currentColor`). Put the primary theme first; a token missing a theme inherits the first theme's value.
5. Run `cd packages/brand && npx vitest run`. It checks the rules above, alias resolution, theme count and text contrast (4.5:1 on the grounds a usage note names).
6. Run `npx oxlint` and `npx oxfmt --check .` in the package, then `just ci` from the repo root before handing off a change that touches Panda.

Why not DTCG: the Claude design system artifact cannot read a name-to-value map (the family shows empty and its entries are lost at the first edit), so the artifact format is the source. A DTCG file would be a generated export for Figma only; there is none yet.

Panda reads these files through `packages/foundations`. Check both Orin themes (dark, light) and both techworx modes (outline, preview) after a colour change. There are no copies: foundations imports the two files directly (`packages/foundations/src/brandFiles.ts`). The old `semantic.json` is kept only as `test/fixtures/semantic.legacy.json`, so the fold test in `test/helpers.ts` can show that no role changed value. Check the generated CSS after a token change by running Panda's `cssgen` for the projects that use it.

## Add or change a mark

1. Masters are in `shared/marks/` (`mark/`, `tools/`, `techworx/mark/`) with the spec in `shared/marks/marks.spec.json`. They are source files; edit them deliberately and diff the result.
2. Follow `docs/brand/principles/shared.md`: one cut (40 regular, 64 small), corner radius 12 (7 on sharp points, concave sharp), keyline 448, optical size target, small master rebuilt heavier, dark-mode irradiation offset.
3. Generators are in `shared/scripts/`. Every path comes from `paths.py` (`MARKS`, `FONTS`, `OUT`, `CACHE`); do not hard-code a root. Setup and run order are in `shared/scripts/README.md`.
4. Scripts write to `packages/brand/build/` only, which is gitignored. Never write into `shared/marks` from a script; copy a result in by hand once you have checked it.
5. Run the spec pipeline in order (`compare.py`, `v2build.py`, `specs.py`, `small_mark.py`, `specs_html.py`) and diff `build/mark-specs/marks.spec.json` against the committed one by hand. The committed spec is never overwritten.
6. Check light and dark side by side at 16, 32 and 64px against a neighbouring mark.

## Generated: do not hand-edit or commit

Everything under `packages/brand/build/`, `.pkl` caches, `mark-specs.html`, reference PNGs, construction SVGs, social cards and exported mark files. Change the source or the script and regenerate. `shared/scripts/github/about/plan.py --apply` edits live GitHub repos; do not run it without being asked.

## Checks that must pass

- `cd packages/brand && npx vitest run`
- `npx oxlint` and `npx oxfmt --check .` in the package
- Spec pipeline completes offline (the `github/` renders also need Chrome)
- Both themes of any mark you changed, viewed side by side

## Claude design system artifact

The Orin DX and techworx.dev design system artifacts are not synced from this package yet; syncing is manual and not automated. Today the library prose is newer than the artifacts in places (Orin layout values, voice rules), and the artifacts carry content with no source here (cover, component previews, links, `lastChange` history). When syncing is set up: write the index last, keep `createdOnFiles` and the asset records, and note that `editing: "code"` makes the page read-only and replaces every file on each sync. Components are the real Astro ones in `packages/components`; do not move the hand-built artifact bundle here.

The source `tokens.json` stays complete because Panda reads it. `shared/scripts/stage_artifact.py` stages a fitted derived copy for the artifact (aliases resolved, role families merged, 12 families, 60 tokens each) and lists anything it cannot represent under `notRepresented` in `upload-manifest.json`; today only the ten `roleStep` duplicates. Never trim the source to fit the artifact, and run `npx vitest run` (`test/artifactFit.test.ts`) after a token change.

## Where history lives

The old library is `~/Projects/orin-dx-site/brand`. It is read-only history: explorations, renders, backups, hand-built component bundle, static brand books. Nothing here depends on it at runtime, and nothing in it should be edited. The historical decisions log is copied to `docs/brand/README.md`.

# https://moonrepo.dev/docs/config/tasks
# Tasks every project inherits, one definition per verb. A project that has nothing to run for a verb opts out with
# `workspace.inheritedTasks.exclude` in its moon.yml; one whose tool differs overrides the task there. Verb-specific
# tasks live beside this file: `vitest.yml` (test) and `panda.yml` (the extra `lint` inputs of projects with a Panda
# config). Apps add build, dev and preview in their own moon.yml.
$schema: 'https://moonrepo.dev/schemas/tasks.json'

fileGroups:
  sources:
    - 'src/**/*'
  tests:
    - '**/*.test.*'
  configs:
    - '*.config.*'
    - '*.json'
  # Every workspace package's source. Packages and apps import each other's source directly, so a task that compiles or

1	import type { Diagnostic } from 'caliper-docgen-napi'
2	import type { DiagnosticLevel } from './diagnostics.js'
3	
4	export interface CaliperDocgenOptions {
5	  srcDirs: string[]
6	  exclude?: string[]
7	  /** Leave out the HTML attributes a component inherits from its element. Same as `htmlAttributes: 'none'`. */
8	  skipHtmlProps?: boolean
9	  /** Which HTML attributes to list: all of them (`'full'`, the default), a compact subset (`'curated'`: handlers, `aria-*`, `ref`, common attributes) or none. Wins over `skipHtmlProps`. */
10	  htmlAttributes?: 'curated' | 'full' | 'none'
11	  /**
12	   * The least severe extraction diagnostic to log, once each: `'error'`, `'warn'` (the default), `'info'`, or
13	   * `'silent'` to log none.
14	   */
15	  logLevel?: DiagnosticLevel
16	  /** Called once for every diagnostic, whatever `logLevel` is. */
17	  onDiagnostic?: (diagnostic: Diagnostic) => void
18	  /** Assign each component its react-docgen-typescript docs as `__docgenInfo`, for Storybook without a docgen server. */
19	  injectDocgenInfo?: boolean
20	  /**
21	   * Read and write the on-disk caches under `node_modules/.cache`. Default: `true`; `false` reads and writes nothing
22	   * there and parses everything every run. The output is the same.
23	   */
24	  cache?: boolean
25	  /** Load the type declarations your props reference from installed packages. On by default; `false` skips it. */
26	  loadDependencies?: boolean
27	  /**
28	   * Which inherited sources of more than 30 props to list as one inherited layer instead of prop by prop: those from
29	   * loaded dependencies (the default), every inherited source, or none.
30	   */
31	  collapseInheritedProps?: 'dependencies' | 'all' | 'none'
32	}

1	import { describe, expect, test } from 'vitest'
2	import { brandTokens, orinPreset, techworxPreset, type Brand } from './index.ts'
3	import { sizeValue } from './scales.ts'
4	import { foldAt } from './fold.ts'
5	import { compactAt } from './ui/popup/presentation.ts'
6	
7	// The two width steps are the whole width vocabulary of a page: tablet and desktop, both min-width. Conditions written as
8	// max-width or with `width <=` bring back an inclusive "narrow" boundary, so a new one fails here.
9	
10	const stepsOf = (preset: typeof orinPreset) => {
11	  const theme = preset.theme?.extend
12	  return { breakpoints: theme?.breakpoints ?? {}, containers: theme?.containers ?? {} }
13	}
14	
15	const maxWidthConditions = (brand: Brand) =>
16	  Object.entries(brandTokens(brand).conditions)
17	    .filter(([, value]) => typeof value === 'string' && /max-width|width\s*<=/u.test(value))
18	    .map(([name]) => name)
19	
20	describe('the two width steps', () => {
21	  test.each([
22	    ['orin', orinPreset],
23	    ['twx', techworxPreset],
24	  ] as const)('%s defines exactly tablet and desktop, for breakpoints and containers', (brand, preset) => {
25	    const { breakpoints, containers } = stepsOf(preset)
26	    expect(Object.keys(breakpoints)).toStrictEqual(['tablet', 'desktop'])
27	    expect(Object.keys(containers)).toStrictEqual(['tablet', 'desktop'])
28	    expect(breakpoints).toStrictEqual(containers)
29	    expect(Object.values(breakpoints)[0]).toBe(sizeValue(brand, 'compactAt'))
30	  })
31	
32	  test.each(['orin', 'twx'] as const)('%s has no max-width or "width <=" condition', (brand) => {
33	    expect(maxWidthConditions(brand)).toStrictEqual([])
34	  })
35	
36	  test.each(['orin', 'twx'] as const)('the presentation chooser agrees with the %s tablet step', (brand) => {
37	    expect(`${compactAt}px`).toBe(sizeValue(brand, 'compactAt'))
38	  })
39	})
40	
41	describe('the default fold width', () => {
42	  test.each(['orin', 'twx'] as const)(
43	    '%s has one fold token and one container condition that read the same width',
44	    (brand) => {
45	      const { conditions, tokens } = brandTokens(brand)
46	      expect(tokens.sizes.fold?.value).toBe(foldAt)
47	      expect(conditions.fromFold).toBe(`@container (width >= ${foldAt})`)
48	    },
49	  )
50	
51	  test.each(['orin', 'twx'] as const)('%s no longer defines the compact and single conditions', (brand) => {
52	    const names = Object.keys(brandTokens(brand).conditions)
53	    expect(names).not.toContain('compact')
54	    expect(names).not.toContain('single')
55	  })
56	})
57	
58	describe('the touch conditions', () => {
59	  test.each(['orin', 'twx'] as const)('%s answers a coarse primary or any attached pointer', (brand) => {
60	    expect(brandTokens(brand).conditions.coarse).toBe('@media (pointer: coarse), (any-pointer: coarse)')
61	  })
62	})

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Snapshot Entire review findings for one or more repositories and summarize them.

Subcommands (standard library only; `pull` needs the `entire` CLI, logged in, with network access):

  pull     Write every finding (open, resolved, dismissed) on every change of the given repositories to a JSON file.
  summary  Print counts per repository by status and severity, changes with findings, and findings per change,
           for one snapshot or for two snapshots side by side (before and after).

Examples:
  python3 tools/entire-findings.py pull --project gh/orin-dx --repos caliper callisto monokl --out findings-2026-11-06.json
  python3 tools/entire-findings.py summary findings-2026-11-06.json
  python3 tools/entire-findings.py summary before.json after.json
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import collections
import json
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

STATUSES = ("open", "resolved", "dismissed")


def entire(*args: str) -> Any:
    done = subprocess.run(["entire", *args, "--json"], capture_output=True, text=True)
    if done.returncode:
        raise SystemExit(f"entire {' '.join(args)}: {done.stderr.strip()[-300:]}")
    return json.loads(done.stdout)


def trail_numbers(project: str, repo: str) -> list[int]:
    numbers: set[int] = set()
    for status in ("open", "closed"):
        token = None
        while True:
            args = ["trail", "list", "--project", project, "--repo", f"{project}/{repo}", "--status", status, "--limit", "100"]
            if token:
                args += ["--page-token", token]
            page = entire(*args)
            numbers.update(item["number"] for item in page.get("items", []))
            token = page.get("nextPageToken")
            if not token:
                break
    return sorted(numbers)


def pull(project: str, repos: list[str]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    changes: dict[tuple[str, str, int], str] = {}
    for repo in repos:
        for number in trail_numbers(project, repo):
            shown = entire("trail", "show", str(number), "--project", project, "--repo", f"{project}/{repo}")
            for change in shown.get("changes", []):
                changes[(repo, change.get("repository", repo), change["number"])] = change.get("branch", "")
    rows: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    for (repo, name, number), branch in sorted(changes.items()):

    for (repo, name, number), branch in sorted(changes.items()):

                        "reason": finding.get("statusReason"),
                    }
                )
    return rows


def summarize(rows: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    by_repo: dict[str, collections.Counter] = collections.defaultdict(collections.Counter)
    per_change: collections.Counter = collections.Counter()
    for row in rows:
        by_repo[row["repo"]][f"status:{row['status']}"] += 1
        by_repo[row["repo"]][f"severity:{row['severity']}"] += 1
        per_change[row["change"]] += 1
    return {
        "total": len(rows),
        "by_repo": {repo: dict(counts) for repo, counts in sorted(by_repo.items())},
        "changes_with_findings": len(per_change),
        "median_per_change_with_findings": sorted(per_change.values())[len(per_change) // 2] if per_change else 0,
        "top_changes": per_change.most_common(5),
    }


def load(path: str) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    return json.loads(Path(path).read_text())


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
    pulled = sub.add_parser("pull")
    pulled.add_argument("--project", required=True)
    pulled.add_argument("--repos", nargs="+", required=True)
    pulled.add_argument("--out", required=True)
    summed = sub.add_parser("summary")
    summed.add_argument("snapshots", nargs="+")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    if args.command == "pull":
        rows = pull(args.project, args.repos)
        Path(args.out).write_text(json.dumps(rows, indent=1))
        print(f"wrote {len(rows)} findings to {args.out}")
        return 0
    for path in args.snapshots:
        print(path)
        print(json.dumps(summarize(load(path)), indent=1))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
